name: AP Micro and Macro Economics (Combined Track)
description: Comprehensive 4-month College Board Advanced Placement (AP) Economics track integrating both AP Microeconomics and AP Macroeconomics into a single cohesive curriculum. Designed with teacher-directed modular flexibility: faculty mentors can customize the pacing sequence to teach Microeconomics first, Macroeconomics first, or concurrently based on student diagnostic assessment. Features rigorous conceptual foundations, mathematical models, dual-graph mastery, real-world case analysis, and extensive College Board FRQ & MCQ exam preparation.
prerequisites: High School Algebra I & Graphical Foundations

modules.title: AP Microeconomics (Individual Markets, Firm Behavior & Efficiency)
modules.description: Complete College Board AP Microeconomics curriculum (Units 1-6). Covers supply and demand mechanics, consumer choice, production costs across market structures, factor markets, and market failure solutions.

topics.title: Unit 1: Basic Economic Concepts & Comparative Advantage
topics.description: Scarcity, opportunity cost, Production Possibilities Curve (PPC), specialization, comparative vs. absolute advantage, terms of trade, and marginal analysis.

topics.title: Unit 2: Supply, Demand, Elasticity & Market Equilibrium
topics.description: Law of demand and supply, determinants of shifts vs. movements, market equilibrium, consumer and producer surplus, price elasticity of demand/supply, cross-price and income elasticity, government interventions (price ceilings, price floors, per-unit/lump-sum taxes, subsidies, tariffs) and deadweight loss.
subtopics: Demand & Supply Shifts vs. Quantity Changes

topics.title: Unit 3: Production, Cost Curves & Perfect Competition
topics.description: Production functions, law of diminishing marginal returns, short-run costs (FC, VC, TC, MC, AFC, AVC, ATC), long-run economies and diseconomies of scale, profit maximization rule (MR=MC), shut-down condition, short-run vs. long-run equilibrium in Perfect Competition, allocative and productive efficiency.
subtopics: Cost Curves: Marginal, Average & Total Costs
Allocative vs. Productive Efficiency & Zero Economic Profit

topics.title: Unit 4: Imperfect Competition & Game Theory
topics.description: Monopoly price-making and deadweight loss, price discrimination, natural monopolies and regulation, Monopolistic Competition in short and long run, Oligopoly interdependence, payoff matrices, dominant strategies, and Nash Equilibrium.
subtopics: Game Theory: Payoff Matrix, Dominant Strategy & Nash Equilibrium

topics.title: Unit 5: Factor Markets & Resource Allocation
topics.description: Derived demand for factors of production, Marginal Revenue Product (MRP) and Marginal Factor Cost (MFC), profit-maximizing hiring rule, perfectly competitive vs. monopsonistic labor markets.
subtopics: Monopsonistic Labor Markets vs. Competitive Labor Markets

topics.title: Unit 6: Market Failure & The Role of Government
topics.description: Socially optimal vs. market output, negative and positive externalities, per-unit corrective taxes and subsidies, public goods vs. private goods, free-rider problem, asymmetric information, income inequality and the Lorenz curve.
subtopics: Public Goods, Club Goods & Free-Rider Problem
Income Inequality, Gini Coefficient & Lorenz Curve

modules.title: AP Macroeconomics (National Economy, Financial System, Stabilization & International Finance)
modules.description: Complete College Board AP Macroeconomics curriculum (Units 1-6). Covers macroeconomic indicators (GDP, CPI, Unemployment), Aggregate Demand/Aggregate Supply, monetary and fiscal policy mechanics, the Phillips curve, and open-economy international exchange.

topics.title: Unit 1: Basic Macroeconomic Concepts & Circular Flow
topics.description: Macroeconomic scope, the circular flow model of income and expenditures, scarcity and resource allocation in national economies, real vs. nominal economic variables.
subtopics: Real vs. Nominal Variables & Base Year Pricing

topics.title: Unit 2: Economic Indicators & The Business Cycle
topics.description: GDP measurement (expenditure approach, what is included/excluded), unemployment rate, labor force participation, frictional/structural/cyclical unemployment, natural rate of unemployment (NRU), inflation, Consumer Price Index (CPI), GDP deflator, costs of inflation, and phases of the business cycle.
subtopics: Gross Domestic Product (GDP): Nominal, Real & Deflator
Unemployment: Categories, Natural Rate & Full Employment
Inflation, CPI, Basket Cost & Cost of Living
The Business Cycle: Peaks, Troughs, Recession & Output Gaps

topics.title: Unit 3: National Income & Price Determination (AD-AS Framework)
topics.description: Aggregate Demand (AD) and its downward slope, shifts in AD, Short-Run Aggregate Supply (SRAS) and sticky wages, Long-Run Aggregate Supply (LRAS) and full employment output, recessionary and inflationary output gaps, spending multiplier and tax multiplier, discretionary fiscal policy and automatic stabilizers.
subtopics: Macroeconomic Equilibrium: Recessionary vs. Inflationary Gaps
Fiscal Policy: Expansionary vs. Contractionary Interventions

topics.title: Unit 4: Financial Sector, Central Banking & Monetary Policy
topics.description: Financial assets (money, bonds, stocks), time value of money, definitions of money (M1, M2), commercial banking and balance sheets (T-accounts), fractional reserve banking and money multiplier, Central Bank policy tools in limited-reserves vs. ample-reserves regimes (IORB, policy rates, discount rate, reserve requirements), the money market graph vs. the loanable funds market graph.
subtopics: Financial Assets, Money Supply (M1/M2) & Time Value
Fractional Reserve Banking, T-Accounts & Money Multiplier
Money Market Model & Nominal Interest Rates
Loanable Funds Market & Real Interest Rates
Monetary Policy in Limited vs. Ample Reserves Regimes

topics.title: Unit 5: Long-Run Consequences of Stabilization Policies
topics.description: Short-run vs. long-run Phillips curve, trade-off between inflation and unemployment, government budget deficits and national debt, crowding-out effect on real interest rates and capital investment, determinants of economic growth and shifts in the LRAS / PPC.
subtopics: Government Deficits, National Debt & Crowding Out
Economic Growth, Human Capital & Physical Capital Formation

topics.title: Unit 6: Open Economy — International Trade and Finance
topics.description: Balance of Payments accounts: Current Account (trade balance) and Capital/Financial Account, foreign exchange (FOREX) market demand and supply of currencies, appreciation and depreciation, determinants of exchange rates, net capital flows and foreign currency linkage with domestic loanable funds.
subtopics: Balance of Payments: Current vs. Financial Account
Real Exchange Rates, Capital Inflow/Outflow & Interest Linkages

modules.title: Teacher-Directed Pacing, Dual Graph Mastery & AP Exam Strategy
modules.description: Flexible modular roadmap allowing faculty mentors to choose the optimal teaching sequence (Micro-First, Macro-First, or Concurrent). Includes side-by-side graph synthesis, official College Board FRQ rubrics, calculator-free arithmetic, and timed full-length simulations.

topics.title: Teacher-Decided Sequencing & Diagnostic Planning
topics.description: Mentor evaluates student background to choose Path A (Microeconomics first then Macroeconomics), Path B (Macroeconomics first then Microeconomics), or Path C (Concurrent parallel tracking).

topics.title: Dual Graph Mastery & Free-Response (FRQ) Scoring Workshop
topics.description: Synthesis of the core 14 essential AP graphs (PPC, Supply/Demand, Cost Curves, Monopoly, Factor Market, AD-AS, Money Market, Loanable Funds, Phillips Curve, FOREX). High-scoring FRQ step-by-step writing strategies and full-length College Board mock exams.
subtopics: Core 14 AP Economics Graphs Side-by-Side Workshop
College Board FRQ Structure, Assertion-Reason & Justifications
Timed Full-Length Micro & Macro Practice Simulations
